summary:
[  edit  ]
The Join  CHOP  takes all its inputs and appends one  CHOP  after another. It is expected they all have the same channels.
The end section of the first  CHOP  is overlapped with the start section of the second  CHOP , and so on for the rest of the input CHOPs. The second input is shifted to line up with the end of the first.
Blending allows you to splice channels together by slowly phasing out one  CHOP  while phasing into the next, or by inserting interpolation curves between the channels of the adjacent CHOPs.
Quaternion Blend blends rotation triplets (rx ry rz) together using the shortest rotation arc. Rotation triplets are identified by "quaternion" attributes, which are set in the  Attribute CHOP .
Translation Blending blends translation channels together by slowly changing from the final velocity of the previous channel to the initial velocity of the next. The next channel may be shifted up or down. If this is undesirable, use cubic blending instead (in the Shape menu). Translation Blending is done on channel triplets that represent translations or positions (*tx *ty *tz).

parameters.label: Method
parameters.name: blendmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - The blend method to produce a seamless sequence:

parameters.label: Preserve Length
parameters.name: pre
parameters.description: The total length of the CHOPs is constant.

parameters.label: Overlap Sequences
parameters.name: ovl
parameters.description: Overlaps the current  CHOP  with the prior  CHOP . Better for audio.

parameters.label: Insert Blend Region
parameters.name: ins
parameters.description: Inserts a region between the CHOPs where the blending is done.

parameters.label: Shape
parameters.name: blendfunc
parameters.description: ⊞  - The blend interpolation shape to use. See Shape in the  Cycle CHOP .

parameters.label: First Input Specifies Blend Regions
parameters.name: blendbyinput
parameters.description: When this is checked on, the first input can be a multi-channel input which specifies blend regions for the remaining inputs into the Join  CHOP . Channel 1 of input0 is used to blend between input1 & input2, channel 2 between input2 & input3, and so on. If not enough channels are specified, the last channel is repeated.

parameters.label: Region
parameters.name: blendregion
parameters.description: The size of the blend region.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.name: blendbias
parameters.description: Which segment to favour when blending: the previous (-1), the next (+1) or neither (0).

parameters.label: Match by
parameters.name: match
parameters.description: ⊞  - Match channels between inputs by index or by name.

parameters.label: Step
parameters.name: step
parameters.description: If set to 1, the next segment will be shifted up or down so that it begins where the last segment ended.

parameters.label: Step  Scope
parameters.name: stepscope
parameters.description: The names of channels that use Step.

parameters.label: Blend  Scope
parameters.name: blendscope
parameters.description: The names of the channels that should be blended. Other channels will not be blended.

parameters.label: Translate X Blend
parameters.name: transscopex
parameters.description: The names of channels that will be translation-blended. Each string field contains a list of its component channels, such as *tx, *ty and *tz.

parameters.label: Translate Y Blend
parameters.name: transscopey
parameters.description: The names of channels that will be translation-blended. Each string field contains a list of its component channels, such as *tx, *ty and *tz.

parameters.label: Translate Z Blend
parameters.name: transscopez
parameters.description: The names of channels that will be translation-blended. Each string field contains a list of its component channels, such as *tx, *ty and *tz.

parameters.label: Quaternion Blend
parameters.name: quatrot
parameters.description: Use quaternion blending on rotation channels.

parameters.label: Shortest  Path  Rotation Blending
parameters.name: shortrot
parameters.description: If enabled, compensates.

parameters.label: Rotation  Scope
parameters.name: rotscope
parameters.description: Enabled when Shortest  Path  Rotation Blending is turned on.

parameters.label: Cycle Length
parameters.name: cyclelen
parameters.description: Enabled when Shortest  Path  Rotation Blending is turned on.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.
